title: Tap Bridge

serves.summary: The learner builds a bridge from metal, wood, sponge or blanket so a soft tap reaches a listener or does not, which shows that hard solids carry sound and soft materials do not.

request.objective: Predict which material will carry a soft tap to a listener and which will not: hard solids such as metal and wood carry it, soft materials such as sponge and blanket do not, and metal carries it farther than wood. NGSS 1-PS4-1 (SCI001-03-b)

problems.ask: The squirrel taps very softly. Help the bunny hear the taps.
problems.goal: The wood bridge is in the gap: wood carries the tap to the bunny's post. Sponge and blanket soak it up, and the air in an empty gap is not enough for a soft tap.

lanes.listener: a bunny who wants to hear the taps

problems.ask: Build a bridge that will not carry the taps to the sleeping cat.
problems.goal: The sponge bridge is in the gap: it soaks up the tap. Metal and wood would carry it to the cat.

problems.ask: The bunny is far away now. Help the bunny hear the soft taps.
problems.goal: The metal bridge is in the gap: metal carries the tap the whole long way. Wood loses too much over this distance.

problems.ask: Help the far-away bunny hear the soft taps.
problems.goal: The thin wire is in the gap: a tight metal wire carries the tap far. The big sponge is thick but soaks the tap up.
